explain.say: Have you noticed that mornings feel cool but afternoons feel hot? A line graph can show that! Look at the board: the line climbs, reaches a peak, then falls again, just like the temperature on a sunny day.

explain.say: The line along the bottom is called the x-axis, and it shows the time of day. The line up the side is the y-axis, and it shows the temperature. Early morning is on the left, low down, because it is cool. Can you find the lowest part of the line?

faq.q: How do I read a line graph?
faq.a: Find the time you want on the bottom axis, go straight up to the line, then across to the side axis to read the value. Where the line goes up, the amount is growing.
asks: How do I read a graph?

faq.q: What do the axes of a graph mean?
faq.a: The axes are the two lines at the edges. The x-axis along the bottom shows one thing, like time, and the y-axis up the side shows another, like temperature.

faq.q: Why is it hottest in the afternoon?
faq.a: The Sun is highest at about midday, but the ground and air keep soaking up its heat for a few more hours. So the warmest time is usually the early afternoon.

faq.q: What is the peak of a graph?
faq.a: The peak is the highest point of the line. On a temperature graph, it shows the hottest time of the day.

faq.q: When should I use a line graph?
faq.a: Use a line graph to show how something changes over time, like the temperature through a day, or a plant growing week by week.
asks: What is a line graph for?

facts: On a sunny day, the warmest time is usually in the early afternoon, not at noon.
A line graph shows how one amount changes as another, often time, goes on.

quiz.say: On a temperature line graph, the line goes down. What does that mean?
quiz.show: On a temperature line graph, the line goes down. What does that mean?
quiz.why: Going down on the temperature axis means the temperature is falling.

wrong.0: Getting hotter would make the line go up.
wrong.1: Time always moves forward along the bottom axis.

quiz.say: At 6 am it was 18 degrees, and at 3 pm it was 30 degrees. How much warmer was 3 pm?
quiz.show: At 6 am it was 18 degrees, and at 3 pm it was 30 degrees. How much warmer was 3 pm?

wrong.1: 48 adds the temperatures instead of finding the difference.
wrong.2: 3 is the hour, not the difference.
